name: Rice Pudding
summary: Rice baked slowly in milk until creamy, stirred to keep the skin in, after Fannie Farmer.

equipment.help: This is a long slow bake, so what matters is how steady your oven is down low.
equipment.label: Oven

steps.title: Wash the rice
steps.body: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear.

steps.title: Mix the pudding
steps.body: Stir the rice, milk, sugar and salt together in a buttered baking dish.

steps.title: Grate the nutmeg over
steps.body: Scatter the nutmeg across the surface and dot with the butter.

steps.title: Heat a gas oven to 300°F
steps.body: Gas cycles on and off. Put the dish in the middle, away from the burner.

steps.title: Heat an electric oven to 300°F
steps.body: Electric ovens hold a low heat well, which suits this pudding.

steps.title: Heat a convection oven to 275°F
steps.body: Drop the heat for the fan, and expect the skin to form sooner.

steps.title: Bake and stir
steps.body: Bake slowly, stirring the skin back in three times during the first hour.
steps.note: Stirring the skin back in is what makes the pudding creamy rather than watery.

steps.title: Let the skin form
steps.body: Stop stirring and let the top brown for the last of the baking.

steps.title: Test it
steps.body: The rice should be soft and the pudding creamy, still a little loose. It thickens as it cools.

steps.title: Serve warm or cold
steps.body: Good either way, plain or with cream.
